keyPhrases.text: There is no better Broadway 'name' for it
feels too small, too meager, and not magic enough
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory needs to go big, surely, or not at all
feels a little lost on the stage
A pressing narrative problem presents itself
are not as vivid as they should be on stage
One wonders how much money was left

reasoning: Despite praising individual performances (Borle, Flynn, Hoffman), the review criticizes fundamental aspects: production feels 'too small,' has 'pressing narrative problems,' pacing issues in Act One, and lacks the necessary spectacle. The ending suggests budget constraints affected quality. More structural criticisms than praise.
